overall_summary: Exoplanet-focused content, particularly detailing extreme weather conditions or 'What If' survival scenarios on hostile planets (e.g., Burning Ice, Darker Than Coal, Supersonic Rubies), consistently outperforms psychology, brain, and basic animal facts. Audiences respond strongly to high-stakes cosmic curiosity and extreme planetary conditions.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Exoplanet Weather & Cosmic Survival Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), TrES-2b 'Darker Than Coal' (1,025 views), and 'What If You Fell Into...' scenarios (948 & 493 views) dominate the channel's top performance tier.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space phenomena, specifically focusing on hostile exoplanets, using 'What If' framing to place the viewer directly in the environment.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' struggled across multiple uploads (5, 10, and 53 views) and 'Songs Stuck in Your Head' failed to gain traction (17 and 71 views).
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic cognitive psychology facts unless they can be framed with a highly dramatic, cinematic narrative hook.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet of Molten Iron Rain?
next_video.opening_direction: Show a cinematic render of a dark planet with glowing red clouds, starting with: 'If you fell onto WASP-76b, the rain wouldn't wet your skin—it would melt right through it.'
next_video.twist_direction: Explain that because one side of the planet permanently faces its star, iron vaporizes, blows to the cold side, and condenses into actual liquid metal showers.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven success of exoplanet weather concepts ('Burning Ice', 'Supersonic Rubies') combined with the high-retention 'What If' survival format.

experiment: Test a 3-part micro-series comparing the '3 Deadliest Planets in the Universe' using a countdown format to increase viewer swipe-through rate and session duration.
